# Nested config keys

`config-keys.md` lists the top-level keys and stops there. The 347 keys below are the documented **sub-keys** -- the level where a feature is actually configured.

`get_key_doc("attention_checks.frequency")` returns any of these individually.

Read this before configuring a block. Guessing a plausible sub-key name and running `potato validate --strict` works for most blocks, but not for the ones listed at the end, where a typo is silent.

## `ai_budget`

Cost estimate and spend cap for AI actions. The complaint about commercial platforms is not the price but the surprise -- credits consumed by auto-labelling and discovered at export time

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cap_usd` | number |  | Dollar ceiling for this project's AI spend. A run projected to cross it is refused BEFORE it starts, so it cannot leave a part-labelled dataset and a bill for it |

## `ai_support`

Model-backed label suggestions shown alongside each item

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ai_config` | object |  | Everything about the model itself: model, base_url, api_key, max_tokens, temperature, timeout, include. One level deeper than the obvious guess — ai_support.model is not read |
| `ai_config.api_base` | string |  | Older spelling of base_url, accepted by the openai_vision endpoint |
| `ai_config.api_key` | string |  | Key for a commercial endpoint. Not needed when base_url points at a self-hosted server; openai and openai_vision also read OPENAI_API_KEY from the environment |
| `ai_config.base_url` | string |  | An OpenAI-compatible server to use instead of the vendor's: vLLM, SGLang, LM Studio, llama.cpp, LiteLLM. Setting it also makes api_key optional, because self-hosted servers do not have one |
| `ai_config.classes` | array |  | Detection classes to keep, by name. Anything else the detector finds is dropped (yolo) |
| `ai_config.confidence_threshold` | number |  | Lowest detection score kept |
| `ai_config.custom_classes` | array |  | Open-vocabulary class names for a detector that accepts them, instead of its trained label set |
| `ai_config.default_video_fps` | number |  | Frame rate assumed when a video does not declare one |
| `ai_config.detail` | string | `auto` | How much of the image the model is charged for: low, high or auto (openai_vision) |
| `ai_config.device` | string |  | Where a local model runs: cpu, cuda, mps |
| `ai_config.enabled` | boolean | `True` | Read by the visual endpoints as a per-endpoint off switch, leaving the rest of ai_support in place |
| `ai_config.include` | object |  | Which schemes get assistants. Off by default: without it every assistant button is absent and the page renders an empty ai-help div |
| `ai_config.include.all` | boolean | `False` | Show assistants on every scheme. This is the switch most authors want, and nothing warns when it is missing |
| `ai_config.include.special_include` | object |  | Per-page, per-scheme assistant list, keyed page number -> annotation id -> list of assistant names. Use instead of include.all to show assistants on some schemes only |
| `ai_config.iou_threshold` | number |  | Overlap above which two detections are treated as the same object |
| `ai_config.json_mode` | boolean | `True` | Ask the server to constrain output to JSON. Servers without constrained decoding reject it; the endpoint notices and retries without, so this rarely needs setting (openai_vision) |
| `ai_config.max_frames` | integer |  | Most frames sampled from a video for one request |
| `ai_config.max_image_size` | integer |  | Longest edge, in pixels, an image is downscaled to before it is sent |
| `ai_config.max_tokens` | integer | `800` | Cap on the reply. The multi-label formats (a rationale or a keyword set for every label) need several hundred; below that the reply is cut off and the assistant renders empty |
| `ai_config.model` | string |  | Model name as the backend spells it |
| `ai_config.temperature` | number | `0.1` | Sampling temperature, 0 to 2 |
| `ai_config.think` | boolean | `False` | Let a reasoning model emit its thinking block. Off keeps the reply to the answer (vllm) |
| `ai_config.timeout` | integer | `30` | Seconds to wait for the model |
| `ai_config_file` | string |  | Path to a separate YAML file holding the endpoint settings, so keys stay out of the repo. Its keys are merged FLAT into ai_config, so the file holds model/base_url/api_key directly — a nested ai_config: block inside it becomes ai_config.ai_config and is ignored. endpoint_type is the one key lifted to the ai_support level. A missing file disables AI support with a warning, which `validate --strict` treats as an error |
| `cache_config` | object |  | Disk cache and prefetch for model replies, so an annotator does not wait for a generation the study has already paid for |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Turn AI assistance on. Without an endpoint that starts, the boot log says so and no assistant appears |
| `endpoint_type` | string | `openai` | Which backend to talk to: openai, openai_vision, anthropic, anthropic_vision, gemini, huggingface, ollama, ollama_vision, openrouter, vllm, yolo, sam, sam3 |

## `analytics`

Cost and latency analytics over ingested traces: optional per-model pricing, and the thresholds that raise a regression alert

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pricing` | object |  | Per-model token pricing used to turn token counts into money |
| `thresholds` | object |  | Fractional increases that trip an alert: cost_per_trace (0.5), avg_latency_ms (0.3), and error_rate as absolute percentage points (0.05) |

## `annotation_telemetry`

The drawing-process analogue of keystroke_logging: content-blind telemetry on geometry schemas -- when someone draws, zooms, revises and accepts AI suggestions, never what or where -- and the rubber-stamping screening built on it

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `detection` | object |  | Rubber-stamping detection: `enabled`, `calibrate` and `thresholds` |
| `disclose_to_annotators` | boolean | `True` | Show the recording notice |
| `disclosure_text` | string |  | Replace the default notice |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Record drawing dynamics |
| `exclude_schemas` | array | `[]` | Schemes to leave alone |
| `fidelity` | string | `events` | How much is kept: off, summary (per-annotation statistics only), or events (raw streams as well) |
| `flush_interval_ms` | integer | `10000` | How often the browser posts its buffered events |
| `idle_ms` | integer | `120000` | Gap above which the annotator is charged to idle rather than active time. Two minutes rather than something tighter, because studying a hard image is real work that produces no events at all |
| `include_schemas` | array | `[]` | Schemes to record. Empty means every geometry schema |
| `store_events` | boolean | `True` | Write raw event streams. Does nothing at summary fidelity |

## `authentication`

Identity provider settings for SSO and database-backed accounts

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_local_login` | boolean |  | Keep username/password registration available alongside SSO |
| `allowed_domain` | string |  | Single-domain form of allowed_domains |
| `allowed_domains` | array |  | Email domains permitted to sign in through SSO |

| `user_config_path` | string |  | JSONL file of registered accounts, one {username, password} object per line, with the password stored as salt$hash. Under the default in_memory backend this is the ONLY thing that makes accounts survive a restart: unset, registrations live in memory and every annotator loses their login when the server stops, while their annotations remain in output_annotation_dir. Set it on anything an annotator will come back to |
| `user_identity_field` | string |  | Which claim from the identity provider becomes the Potato username |

## `boundary_probing`

Boundary Lab. After a label is chosen, shows counterfactual edits of the item and asks whether they flip it -- which maps the decision boundary and exports as a contrast set

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ai_support` | object |  | Endpoint override for the llm tier; falls back to the global ai_support block |
| `debounce_ms` | integer | `900` | Delay between choosing a label and fetching probes |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Show probes |
| `include_invariance` | boolean | `True` | Include a meaning-preserving paraphrase probe. A paraphrase that flips the label is the quality-control signal this exists to catch |
| `precomputed_key` | string | `counterfactuals` | Item field holding precomputed counterfactuals, a list of `{text, kind: flip\|invariance}` |
| `probes_per_item` | integer | `3` | Probes per (instance, label), counting the invariance probe |
| `rationale_on_flip` | boolean | `True` | Ask for a short written reason when the annotator says a probe flips their label |
| `schema` | string |  | Scheme whose labels are probed. Defaults to the first radio scheme |
| `sources` | array | `['precomputed', 'llm', 'rules']` | Ordered generation tiers -- precomputed, llm, rules. Earlier tiers win and later ones fill the remaining slots |

## `bws_config`

Best-worst scaling. Builds the tuples annotators compare and scores the results into a ranking. Its presence is what enables BWS

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `min_item_appearances` | integer |  | Times each item must appear across the tuples |
| `num_tuples` | any |  | Tuples generated in total, or null to derive the count from min_item_appearances |
| `scoring` | object |  | Scoring block; `method` selects the estimator (counting by default) |
| `seed` | integer |  | Seed for tuple generation, so a design can be reproduced |
| `tuple_size` | integer |  | Items shown per comparison |

## `calibration`

Agreement drift tracking and the re-calibration prompt on /admin/iaa. Agreement is scored per time window so a fall in recent work is visible, instead of averaging into one whole-project number

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drop_threshold` | number | `0.15` | Relative fall below the project baseline that raises the re-calibration prompt, e.g. 0.15 for 15% |
| `enabled` | boolean | `True` | Compute the agreement timeline. Costs one extra IAA pass per window, so it can be turned off on very large projects |
| `window_by` | string | `count` | 'count' gives every window the same number of items, 'time' the same duration. Equal-count is the default because a study that ran in bursts leaves equal-duration windows empty, and an empty window has no agreement rather than low agreement |
| `windows` | integer | `6` | How many time windows the timeline is cut into |

Group instances into units of analysis -- a participant, an interview -- so codes can be counted per case rather than per item

| `auto_detect` | boolean | `True` | Scan loaded items for cases at startup. Set false to assign cases by hand |
| `enabled` | boolean |  | Turn case grouping on or off explicitly. Unset, it follows qda_mode |
| `key` | string |  | Item field to group on. Unset, detection scans participant_id, respondent_id and case_id |

## `category_assignment`

Route items to annotators by the item's category, optionally gated on a qualification the annotator earned in training

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `category_key` | string |  | Item field holding the category. Must be a non-empty string |
| `dynamic` | object |  | Probabilistic expertise routing, which learns who is good at what from agreement instead of a fixed qualification. Carries its own `enabled` |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Turn category routing on. Also gates the qualification scoring that runs when someone finishes training |
| `fallback` | string | `uncategorized` | What an annotator with no matching qualification is given |
| `qualification` | object |  | How training performance becomes a per-category qualification: `source` (training, prestudy or both), `threshold` (0-1, default 0.7) and `min_questions` (default 1) |

| `knn` | object |  | Neighbour-graph parameters; `k` defaults to 10 |
| `sample_size` | integer |  | Documents sampled into the map |
| `umap` | object |  | UMAP projection parameters |

## `cot_segmentation`

Split a long chain-of-thought string into labelable steps once, at load time, so the cot_trace display and the process_reward scheme read the same cached list

|---|---|---|---|
| `llm_max_chars` | integer |  | Characters of reasoning sent to the model under the llm strategy |
| `markers` | array |  | Separator strings for the markers strategy |
| `max_steps` | integer |  | Hard cap on steps per item, which keeps pathological input from reaching the UI |
| `min_step_chars` | integer |  | Steps shorter than this are merged into the previous one |
| `sentences_per_step` | integer |  | Sentences grouped into one step by the sentence strategy |
| `source_key` | string |  | Item field holding the reasoning string. Required whenever the block is present |
| `strategy` | string | `auto` | How to split: blank_line, numbered, markers, sentence, llm, or auto. llm needs an ai_support or judge_alignment endpoint and falls back to the heuristics if it cannot reach one |
| `target_key` | string | `cot_steps` | Item field the step list is written to. Point the display's and scheme's `steps_key` at this |

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| `cache_size` | integer |  | Items the paged backend keeps in memory |
| `path` | string |  | SQLite file the paged backend uses |

## `keystroke_logging`

Content-blind typing dynamics on free-text fields -- when someone pauses, revises or pastes, never which keys -- and the composed/transcribed/pasted detection built on them

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `classify_paste_source` | boolean | `True` | Try to tell a paste from outside the page from one that only moved text within it |
| `detection` | object |  | Rule-based flags: `enabled`, `calibrate`, `on_external_insert` (allow, warn, block or flag) and `thresholds`. Thresholds are scored server-side and withheld from the browser, which would otherwise tell an annotator exactly how slowly to paste to stay under the flag |
| `disclose_to_annotators` | boolean | `True` | Show the recording notice. Turning it off collects typing dynamics silently, which your consent documents and ethics approval have to cover |
| `disclosure_text` | string |  | Replace the default notice. Must be non-empty; omit it to keep the default |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Record typing dynamics. Off by default: it records how annotators produce free text, so it is opt-in rather than something a project acquires by upgrading Potato |
| `exclude_schemas` | array | `[]` | Schemes to leave alone |
| `fidelity` | string | `events` | How much is kept: off, summary (per-response statistics only), or events (raw streams as well) |
| `flush_interval_ms` | integer | `5000` | How often the browser posts its buffered events |
| `idle_session_ms` | integer | `30000` | Gap that ends one typing session and starts the next |
| `include_schemas` | array | `[]` | Schemes to record. Empty means every free-text field |
| `pause_thresholds_ms` | array | `[500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000]` | Pause buckets the summary counts against. Must be positive integers |
| `store_events` | boolean | `True` | Write raw event streams to the typing store. Does nothing at summary fidelity, which the loader warns about |

## `layout`

How the annotation questions are arranged on the page: a grid, collapsible groups, an explicit order, and responsive breakpoints. Without it every scheme stacks full-width in config order

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `breakpoints` | object |  | Viewport widths, in pixels, where the grid reduces |
| `breakpoints.mobile` | integer | `480` | Below this width the grid collapses to one column |
| `breakpoints.tablet` | integer | `768` | Below this width column spans are reduced |
| `grid` | object |  | Grid the question forms are laid out in |
| `grid.align_items` | string | `start` | Vertical alignment within a row: start, center, end or stretch |
| `grid.columns` | integer | `2` | Columns in the form grid, 1 to 6. A scheme spans one unless its own layout.columns says otherwise |
| `grid.gap` | string | `1rem` | CSS gap between forms, as a string |
| `grid.row_gap` | string |  | CSS gap between rows, when it should differ from gap |
| `groups` | array |  | Collapsible titled sections, each holding named schemes. The way to keep a long question list navigable |
| `groups.background_color` | string |  | CSS colour for this group, overriding the alternating default |
| `groups.collapsed_default` | boolean |  | Start the group folded. Only sensible for questions most items do not need, since a folded question is one annotators skip |
| `groups.collapsible` | boolean |  | Let annotators fold the group away |
| `groups.description` | string |  | Line of explanation under the group heading |
| `groups.id` | string |  | Identifier for the group, unique within layout.groups. Required |
| `groups.schemas` | array |  | Names of the annotation schemes this group holds, in the order they should appear. Required, non-empty, and every name must be a real scheme -- an unknown one fails validation |
| `groups.title` | string |  | Heading shown on the group |
| `order` | array |  | Scheme names in the order they should appear, overriding config order |
| `styling` | object |  | Colours, padding and alignment for groups and forms |
| `styling.align_items` | string | `start` | Vertical alignment of forms inside a group: start, center, end or stretch |
| `styling.content_align` | string | `left` | Horizontal alignment of the content inside a form: left, center or right |
| `styling.form_padding` | string | `0.375rem 0.5rem` | CSS padding inside one question form |
| `styling.group_background_even` | string | `#f8f9fc` | Background colour for even-numbered groups |
| `styling.group_background_odd` | string | `#fafafa` | Background colour for odd-numbered groups |
| `styling.group_padding` | string | `0.5rem 0.75rem` | CSS padding inside a group |

## `live_coding_agent`

Same idea for a coding agent: runs the agent against a repository and streams its tool calls into a live_coding_agent display field

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acknowledge_untrusted_code_execution` | boolean | `False` | Required alongside sandbox_mode: trusted. Confirms you accept that annotator-editable tool calls, including arbitrary shell commands, run directly on this host as the Potato user |
| `ai_config` | object |  | Model settings passed to the backend (model name, endpoint, API key). Server-side only: a request cannot override it, because it carries credentials |
| `backend_type` | string | `ollama_tool_use` | Which agent backend drives the session: ollama_tool_use, anthropic_tool_use, openai_tool_use, claude_sdk |
| `container_cli` | string | `docker` | Container tool to drive: docker or podman. Rootless Podman needs no root daemon |
| `container_runtime` | string |  | Alternative container runtime, passed straight through as --runtime. Use runsc for gVisor (syscall interception in userspace) or kata for a hardware VM boundary. Unset uses the daemon default |
| `max_turns` | integer | `50` | Stop the agent loop after this many turns |
| `sandbox_cpus` | number | `1` | CPU limit for the sandbox container |
| `sandbox_image` | string | `python:3.12-slim` | Image the sandbox container runs. Point this at your own image to give the agent more tooling; pin a digest if you need reproducibility |
| `sandbox_memory` | string | `512m` | Memory limit for the sandbox container, in Docker syntax |
| `sandbox_mode` | string | `container` | Boundary the agent's tool calls run inside: container (Docker or Podman), bubblewrap (Linux hosts without a container runtime), or trusted (no isolation, requires acknowledge_untrusted_code_execution). The former docker, worktree and direct modes are deprecated aliases; worktree never provided isolation |
| `sandbox_network` | string | `none` | Container network mode. Left at none the agent cannot reach the network, so it cannot exfiltrate what it reads |
| `sandbox_pids_limit` | integer | `128` | Maximum processes inside the sandbox container, which caps fork bombs |
| `sandbox_root` | string |  | Directory holding per-session workspace copies. Defaults to a .potato-sandboxes directory beside working_dir |
| `sandbox_user` | string | `65534:65534` | uid:gid the sandboxed tools run as. Defaults to nobody |
| `system_prompt` | string | `""` | Extra system prompt prepended to the agent's instructions |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Repository the agent works on. Copied per session into a sandbox workspace rather than used in place, so agent edits never touch it |

## `login`

Login mode. type: password, url_direct, or none

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string |  | How annotators identify themselves |
| `url_argument` | string |  | Query parameter carrying the user id under url_direct login |

## `mace`

MACE competence estimation: infers per-annotator reliability and a predicted label per item from the disagreement pattern alone

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Run MACE |
| `min_annotations_per_item` | integer | `3` | Items with fewer annotators than this are left out of the fit |
| `min_items` | integer | `5` | Refuse to fit until this many eligible items exist |
| `num_iters` | integer | `50` | EM iterations per restart |
| `num_restarts` | integer | `10` | EM restarts; the best-scoring run is kept |
| `trigger_every_n` | integer | `10` | Refit after this many new annotations |

## `mcp`

Model Context Protocol control surface, letting an agent query and control this running task. Off unless every tool is named explicitly

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_debug` | boolean | `False` | Permit the MCP surface on a debug server. Off by default: debug disables admin authentication server-wide, so the two together are a remote shell |
| `audit_log` | string | `mcp_audit.jsonl` | File recording every MCP call and refusal, one JSON object per line |
| `auth` | object |  | Where per-agent tokens live. `tokens_file` defaults to mcp_tokens.json under task_dir |
| `destructive` | array |  | Second, separate opt-in for tools that discard work. A destructive tool must appear here and in mcp.tools, and callers must pass confirm: true |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Register the /api/mcp/* endpoints. Without this they do not exist |
| `scope` | object |  | Limits on what agents may touch, e.g. `users` to restrict which annotators they can act on |
| `tools` | array |  | Allowlist of tool names an agent may call. Empty grants nothing, and an unrecognized name fails at startup rather than warning |

## `pocket`

Pocket Mode: the phone-sized annotation surface at /pocket, served as a PWA with an offline queue

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto_redirect` | boolean | `True` | Send phones and tablets that open /annotate to /pocket, when every scheme in the task is touch-capable. `?desktop=1` opts back out |
| `batch_size` | integer | `25` | Items per batch request, which is also the offline queue depth. Clamped to 1-200 |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Register the /pocket surface |

## `psychometrics`

Live IRT. Fits item difficulty and annotator ability as labels arrive, so labels carry error bars and confident items can stop early

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `confidence_threshold` | number | `0.95` | Posterior probability at which an item counts as resolved. Outside 0.5-1.0 it is ignored and 0.95 used |
| `cost_per_judgment` | number |  | Cost of one judgment, used to price the saved judgments on the dashboard |
| `discrimination_flag_threshold` | number | `-0.2` | Items whose ability-versus-correctness correlation falls below this are flagged as likely codebook bugs |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Fit the model and serve the dashboard. Adaptive routing additionally needs assignment_strategy: psychometric |
| `min_annotators_per_item` | integer | `2` | Floor before an item may be stopped early, however confident the posterior |
| `min_observations` | integer | `20` | Cold-start gate: routing falls back to random until this many labels exist, so early assignments build the overlap the model needs |
| `refit_interval` | integer | `5` | Refit once this many new labels have arrived since the last fit |
| `schema` | string |  | Scheme the model scores. Defaults to the first radio or likert scheme |

## `qda_mode`

Qualitative data analysis mode. Turning it on moves the defaults for memos, the codebook and case grouping together, rather than each being switched on separately

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `codebook` | object |  | QDA codebook defaults: `enabled` (true) and `mode` (open). Sub-keys of qda_mode are not recursed into, so an unrecognized block is carried through for forward compatibility -- and a typo passes silently |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Master switch for QDA mode |
| `memos` | object |  | QDA memo defaults: `enabled` and `show_sidebar_by_default`, both true. Memo storage itself is universal; this block only sets the QDA defaults |

## `review_mode`

Hotkey review queue. Once the current item is complete the page moves on by itself, which turns keyboard-labelled schemes into press-key-and-advance

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `advance_on` | string | `complete` | What counts as complete: `complete` (every scheme on the page has a value) or `required` (the required-validated ones do) |
| `auto_advance` | boolean | `True` | Advance without being asked. Set false to keep review mode on but navigate by hand |
| `delay_ms` | integer | `350` | Pause between completion and advancing |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Turn review mode on |

## `review_workflow`

Reviewer routing and the kanban board at /admin/review. Keeps its own state per instance (pending, in_review, needs_second, adjudication, done) alongside the annotations

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto_enroll` | boolean | `True` | Enroll every loaded instance at startup. Set false to enroll by hand |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Register the review board |
| `reviewers` | array |  | Reviewer pool that round-robin rules draw from |
| `routing` | array |  | First-match rules of `when` (the shared condition grammar) plus `state`, `priority`, and either `assign_to` or `round_robin` |

## `rooms`

Multiplayer rooms at /rooms: live norming sessions, adjudication huddles and shadowing over a shared event log

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Register the /rooms surface |
| `max_members` | integer | `12` | Members allowed in one room. Clamped to 2-100 |
| `persist_votes` | boolean | `True` | Write a room's final vote into each member's own annotations |
| `poll_interval_ms` | integer | `1500` | How often clients poll for room events. Clamped to 500-30000 |
| `schema` | string |  | Scheme members vote on. Defaults to the first radio or likert scheme; with neither present, rooms disable themselves |
| `who_can_create` | string | `any` | Who may open a room: any member, or admin only |

## `search`

Full-text search over loaded items, backed by SQLite FTS5. Admin search is read-only and always available; annotator search-and-claim is a separate opt-in

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `annotator_claim` | boolean | `False` | Let annotators search the corpus and claim their own next item. Refused at startup when combined with a sampling-dependent assignment strategy or an overlap cap, since self-selection breaks both. Allowed unconditionally under qda_mode/solo_mode |
| `backend` | string | `fts5` | Index backend. fts5 is the only one built in; any other name disables search with a warning |
| `enabled` | boolean | `True` | Build the search index at startup |
| `max_instances` | integer | `100000` | Ceiling on how many instances are indexed |

## `sessions`

Group items into sessions by session_id or thread_id and score the whole session at /sessions. Schemes opt in with `session_level: true`

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attributes` | array |  | Item fields lifted onto the session |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Build sessions at startup |
| `key` | string |  | Item field holding the session id. Unset, detection tries session_id then thread_id, looking inside `metadata` as well as at the top level |

## `solo_mode`

Single-coder loop. An LLM labels the corpus, you review where it is least sure, and the prompt is refined from your corrections

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `batches` | object |  | Batch sizes for LLM labeling: llm_labeling_batch (50) and max_parallel_labels (200) |
| `confidence_routing` | object |  | Where an item goes by confidence band: auto-accept, review, or human |
| `confusion_analysis` | object |  | Confusion-pair analysis over model-versus-human disagreements |
| `edge_case_rules` | object |  | Rules distilled from your corrections and applied before the model |
| `embedding` | object |  | Embedder for diversity and textbox similarity; `model_name` defaults to all-MiniLM-L6-v2 |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Turn solo mode on |
| `instance_selection` | object |  | Weights that decide what you are shown next: low_confidence_weight (0.4), diversity_weight (0.3), random_weight (0.2), disagreement_weight (0.1), and the opt-in edge_case_rule, cartography and llm_predicted weights |
| `labeling_functions` | object |  | Programmatic labeling functions run alongside the model |
| `labeling_models` | array |  | Endpoints that label the corpus. Each is endpoint_type plus model, and optionally api_key, base_url, max_tokens, temperature, think, timeout |
| `prompt_optimization` | object |  | Automatic prompt search: enabled (true), find_smallest_model, target_accuracy (0.85), optimization_interval_seconds, and the accuracy/length/consistency weights |
| `refinement_loop` | object |  | The automatic refine-evaluate-keep cycle over the labeling prompt |
| `refinement_loop.auto_apply_suggestions` | boolean |  | Adopt a winning candidate prompt without asking |
| `refinement_loop.dry_run` | boolean |  | Score candidates but never adopt one |
| `refinement_loop.enabled` | boolean |  | Run the refinement cycle |
| `refinement_loop.max_cycles` | integer |  | Cycles before the loop stops |
| `refinement_loop.require_approval` | boolean |  | Hold a candidate prompt until it is approved, rather than adopting it |
| `refinement_loop.trigger_interval` | integer |  | New human labels between cycles |
| `revision_models` | array |  | Endpoints used to revise the prompt. Defaults to labeling_models |
| `state_dir` | string |  | Where solo-mode state is persisted |
| `thresholds` | object |  | The stopping and agreement thresholds -- including end_human_annotation_agreement (0.90) and minimum_validation_sample (50) -- plus the per-scheme-type match tolerances |
| `uncertainty` | object |  | How model uncertainty is estimated: `strategy` (direct_confidence, direct_uncertainty, token_entropy, sampling_diversity) and a `sampling_diversity` block |

## `thinkaloud`

Think-aloud mode: local speech-to-text over spoken rationales, plus rule-based detection of spoken label phrases

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chunk_seconds` | integer | `6` | Recorder restart interval. Each chunk is a complete audio file so it can be decoded on its own. Clamped to 2-30 |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Record and transcribe rationales |
| `fillers` | array |  | Filler lexicon behind the hesitation signal |
| `language` | string | `en` | Language hint passed to Whisper |
| `model` | string | `tiny.en` | Whisper model size for the faster_whisper backend |
| `require_spoken_label` | boolean | `True` | Nudge on Next when no label was committed by voice |
| `schema` | string |  | Scheme whose labels may be committed by voice. Defaults to the first radio scheme |
| `stems` | array |  | Override the accepted label-phrase stem patterns |
| `stt` | string | `auto` | Speech-to-text backend: faster_whisper (local), mock (tests), or auto |

## `trace_ingestion`

Accept agent traces posted to /api/traces/*

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_unauthenticated` | boolean | `False` | Accept trace posts with no api_key set. Off by default: without it the webhook endpoints reject every request rather than running open |
| `api_key` | string |  | Shared secret for the trace webhooks, accepted as either Authorization: Bearer or X-API-Key |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Register the trace webhook endpoints |
| `notify_annotators` | boolean |  | Push newly ingested traces to connected annotators |
| `sources` | array |  | Upstream trace sources to poll |

## `triage`

Rank items by a priority signal so failures, thumbs-down feedback and low scores get annotated first. Scoring runs as items are added, so it covers traces ingested at runtime as well as loaded files

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `default_priority` | number | `0` | Priority given to items no rule matched |
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Score items into a priority |
| `invert_signal` | boolean | `False` | Negate signal_field, for scores where lower is worse |
| `order` | string | `desc` | Queue direction: desc serves the highest priority first |
| `rules` | array |  | Rules of `when` (the shared condition grammar) plus priority and an optional badge; the highest-priority match wins. Leaving both this and signal_field unset installs built-in rules for errored agents, thumbs-down feedback and scores below 0.5 |
| `show_badge` | boolean | `True` | Show the matching rule's badge on the item |
| `signal_field` | string |  | Item field read as a numeric priority when no rule matches |

## `truth_serum`

Surprisingly-popular scoring. Each annotator also predicts how many others will pick the same label, and an answer that beats its own predicted popularity wins over the majority

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `False` | Ask the prediction question |
| `min_annotators` | integer | `3` | Predictions needed on an item before a surprisingly-popular verdict is computed. Values below 2 are raised to 2 |
| `question` | string |  | Prompt shown above the prediction slider |
| `schema` | string |  | Scheme whose labels get popularity predictions. Defaults to the first radio scheme; with none, predictions stay inactive |

Interface language code

| Key | Type | Default | Description |

| `iaa_drift_codebook_changes` | string |  | Label preceding the list of codebook revisions on the timeline |

| `iaa_drift_title` | string |  | Heading of the agreement-over-time section on /admin/iaa |
| `iaa_drift_untimed` | string |  | Note about items with no timestamp, which cannot be placed on the timeline |

## Blocks whose sub-keys are not checked

`potato validate --strict` fails on an unrecognized sub-key in most blocks. In these it accepts anything, so a misspelled sub-key is silent and the feature is simply off:

- `agent_proxy.*`
- `annotation_schemes.*`
- `automatic_assignment.*`
- `crowdsourcing.*`
- `data_files.*`
- `data_sources.*`
- `dataset_metadata.*`
- `embeddings.*`
- `huggingface_backup.*`
- `icl_labeling.*`
- `instance_reclaim.*`
- `keyword_highlight_settings.*`
- `live_agent.*`
- `llm_labeling.*`
- `mturk.*`
- `partial_loading.*`
- `per_annotator_quota.*`
- `prestudy.*`
- `publish.*`
- `quality_control.*`
- `scheme_sets.*`
- `surveyflow.*`
- `ui.*`
- `ui_config.*`
- `user_roles.*`

Checking is also at most two levels deep everywhere else: `training.feedback` is checked, `training.feedback.anything` is not. Entries inside `annotation_schemes` and `instance_display.fields` are not checked either, which is why `key_binding` in place of `key_value` validates clean and does nothing.
